name: Cloud Account Details
purpose: Identifies whether a local Windows account is actually a Microsoft cloud account by recording the email address tied to it, directly inside the SAM hive.
key_fields: InternetUserName value under the account's RID subkey — contains the email address tied to the Microsoft cloud account
normal_baseline: Accounts known to be signed in with a Microsoft account (personal or Azure AD-backed) show an InternetUserName value matching the expected corporate or personal email; accounts that are genuinely local-only have no InternetUserName value at all.
anomalies: An InternetUserName value present on an account that was assumed to be a local-only service or admin account, indicating undisclosed cloud-account linkage
InternetUserName email domain that doesn't match the organization's expected domain, suggesting a personal Microsoft account was used to sign into a corporate machine
A newly created account with an InternetUserName tied to an external, unfamiliar email address shortly before or during a suspected compromise
anti_forensic_notes: The value only exists if the account was ever configured to sign in with a Microsoft cloud account; a purely local account will simply have no InternetUserName value, which is not itself suspicious. Converting a cloud-linked account back to local removes this value going forward, but historical evidence may still be recoverable from registry hive backups (RegBack) or Volume Shadow Copies.
interpretation: The presence of this value is what distinguishes a Microsoft cloud account from a purely local one at the SAM level — check it whenever you need to know whether a given local username actually authenticates against a Microsoft identity rather than a locally-stored password. Cross-reference the email domain against known-good corporate domains to catch personal-account usage on managed hardware.
